note: Watchlist baseline from the discovery sweep of 18 August 2026 (see watchlist.md). 124 products across 104 terms URLs: 101 readable by plain fetch, 23 needing the agent. Deliberately holds NO RATES — it is a diff anchor for identity and routing only. Every product's lastChecked is null because no collection run has happened yet; the first real sweep sets it and reports changes rather than re-dumping. httpStatus/readable are the values MEASURED on the sweep date, so a later change in either is itself a reportable move (a page going 200 -> 403, or marketing-only -> yes). | 2026-08-18: provider-page matches the FIRST koersopslag on a page, and 4 ICS business cards, 3 ANWB cards, 14 Amex cards and both Knab cards each share one URL - so a page-level match is not yet a product-level fact. Two figures were hand-verified as another row's (see figureNote on abn-amro-betaalpas and knab-creditcard). Row attribution is owed before any task raises coverage from provider-page. | 2026-08-18, MEASURED: the readable flags were recorded with curl, and node's fetch (what the sweep actually uses) disagrees on some hosts. rabobank.nl/particulieren/betalen/betaalproducten/kosten-voorwaarden -> HTTP 200, 459 kB, 32x 'koersopslag', 22 percentage figures, where curl was 403. ing.nl/particulier/betalen/passen/buitenland -> 200, 26 kB (no percentages: shadow DOM). ing.nl spaarrente -> 200. revolut.com legal/standard-fees -> 403 to node too, coinbase.com/nl/card -> 403 to node too. Four URLs measured, not thirteen - do not generalise the rest without measuring them (that is error 3). Rabobank alone is 3 products with a live table, and it is the next slice's cheapest win, but provider-page must learn product-row attribution first or it will read the wrong row off a 22-figure page.
